sentences.text: S2 disclosed that her mother, Margaret (81 years old), has dementia diagnosed two years ago and lives on Larch Road with carers.
S2 disclosed that her brother, Martin, holds the power of attorney for financial and property affairs, which Margaret signed in 2023 and registered.
S2 disclosed that she found a £12,000 transfer from Margaret's account to Martin's account on 14 August, which she photographed and printed.
S2 disclosed that Martin arrived at Margaret's house in a new white estate car in early September.
S2 disclosed that when asked where the money came from, Martin stated Margaret had 'helped him out' and that he is entitled to it because he does everything for her.
S2 disclosed that she knows of no prior gifts from Margaret to Martin before the dementia diagnosis.
S2 disclosed that on 22 September, Margaret told her Martin made her sign a document, though Margaret did not know what it was and was frightened to say no.
S2 disclosed that she has not seen the document Margaret was asked to sign on 22 September and has searched Margaret's drawers without finding it.
S2 disclosed that Margaret's care invoices from the agency 'Brightwell' are three months behind, totaling approximately £2,400.
S2 disclosed that 'Brightwell' wrote to Margaret's address on 3 November stating the agency might stop calls if the debt is not paid.
S2 disclosed that Margaret has a social worker she has never met, and her GP is at the Wexley health centre.
S2 disclosed that she is worried Martin might sell the house, which would leave nothing for Margaret's care.
S2 disclosed that Martin has not said anything about selling the house.
S1 advised that an attorney must act in the client's best interests and keep money separate, and noted that a £12,000 transfer to himself without authority is something the Office,
S1 advised that the Office of the Public Guardian can ask Martin to account for every penny and apply to the Court of Protection to cancel the power of attorney.
S1 advised that taking money as an attorney can be a criminal offence.
S1 advised that Margaret is an adult at risk and recommended an adult safeguarding referral to Wexley council.
S1 advised S2 not to confront Martin about the issue for now, as it could cause him to move more money or become defensive.
S1 advised S2 to ring 'Brightwell' and explain the situation is in hand so calls do not stop.
S1 instructed S2 to email the statement photos and the agency letter by Friday 27 November.
S1 instructed S2 that he would write to the Office of the Public Guardian by Tuesday 1 December.
S1 instructed S2 that he would make the safeguarding referral today (17 November).
S1 instructed S2 to send the client care letter today (17 November).
S1 scheduled a next meeting for 8 December.
